The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Robinhood CEO says companies shouldn't get veto over stock tokens in AMC feud. In a post on Friday, Vlad Tenev said securities issuers should control shareholder rights, but not separate products that track their publicly traded shares. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The legal drama of imprisoned Sam Bankman-Fried is waiting on its last act. The fallen leader of the former top exchange FTX is looking for answers from the U.S. Supreme Court. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

With Fed rate hike all but assured, here's how markets might react. Traders could look past an expected Fed hike and weigh what higher rates are signaling about the economy. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

India's richest state is exploring tokenizing its own assets to fund new infrastructure. Maharashtra is drafting a policy to tokenize the state's assets, including the electricity transmission infrastructure. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Metaplanet cuts executive reward pool by 41%, extinguishes $220 million in value. The bitcoin treasury firm cut the potential Series 10 share pool to 188.2 million. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Zodia Custody CEO Julian Sawyer steps down, becomes adviser. Sawyer will become a strategic adviser rather than take the helm of Zodia Solutions, as previously announced. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $77,259 with a +0.06% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,522.8 with a +2.28% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: GENIUS Act explained: What it means for crypto and digital assets
items.description: Signed into law on July 18, 2025, the historic legislation sets up a regulatory framework for USD-backed payment stablecoins and serves as a crucial first step towards broader digital asset regulatory clarity. While stablecoins are the main focus of the legislation, you’re likely to see effects across the entire digital asset ecosystem. That could mean tailwinds for crypto assets and crypto-related companies, as well as traditional financial companies that will bring their business on chain.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress made progress in 2025 toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. One measure—the GENIUS Act—was signed into law. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

items.title: Geopolitical risks and crypto exchange rate premium: Implications for capital flight
items.description: Geopolitical risks have emerged as a critical force shaping the global economic landscape, with recent events such as the Russia-Ukraine conflict (2022–present), U.S.-China trade tensions, and Middle Eastern escalations highlighting their profound impacts on macroeconomic stability and financial markets (Itakura, 2020; Fajgelbaum and Khandelwal, 2022; Liadze et al., 2023). Despite the growing literature on the economic and financial impacts of geopolitical risk (e.g., Gupta et al., 2019; Wang [...] By employing local projections on a monthly panel dataset of 24 countries from 1/2019 to 1/2025, this paper brings several insights. First, an increase in country-level geopolitical risk in a given month leads to a significant rise in the crypto exchange rate premium in subsequent months. This suggests that localized geopolitical shocks, such as conflicts or sanctions, heighten domestic demand for Bitcoin as a means of capital flight, which drives up local prices relative to global benchmarks. [...] global benchmarks. Second, while the global Geopolitical Threats (GPRT) only exert negligible impacts on the crypto exchange rate premium, the global Geopolitical Acts (GPRA) persistently reduce it. The persistent decline in the premium following GPRA shocks indicates heightened investor caution toward using cryptocurrencies for capital flight during realized geopolitical events. This reduction likely stems from increased global risk aversion and elevated volatility in crypto markets triggered
